angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 398,636 km at 75.46 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.2523 +/- 0.0121 mas (same row, RUWE 1.13): 75.46 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.573 +/- 0.012 solar radii from Artigau et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1278 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..144A/abstract): 398,636 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.54 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Artigau et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1278 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..144A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3799 +/- 42 K from Artigau et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1278 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..144A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Artigau et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1278 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..144A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1278.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.654, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
